parsed.process: Traditional sukumo fermentation indigo vat (living alkaline microbial dye culture)
parsed.process_problem: No instrument tells the craftsperson the vat's health/state; managing the always-changing natural dye solution relies only on years of intuition via the five senses, and vats can 'die' unpredictably with no labeled time-series of trajectories
parsed.recent_technique: Vision-language model zero-shot/few-shot visual anomaly detection (CLIP-based prompting / in-context learning, e.g. FADE, IADGPT, VMAD)
parsed.how_it_improves: Inputs: ordinary RGB or phone photos/video of the vat surface (the 'bloom'/foam pattern, color of the liquor, scum/bubble texture) plus natural-language reference prompts describing a healthy vat ('coppery bronze foam, fine even bubbles, jade-green liquor') versus failure cues ('flat grey surface, broken film, sour-smelling thin froth'). Model: a VLM anomaly detector scores and localizes how far the current surface deviates from the healthy text/visual reference, with a few craftsperson-labeled 'good day' images as in-context support. Actionable output: a continuous deviation score and a heatmap flagging where/when the surface is drifting toward a 'dying' state, days before a master might catch it -- a cheap early-warning dashboard. Gain: turns a tacit five-senses judgment into a sharable, logged signal that lets the dyer intervene (feed lye, wheat bran, warmth) before collapse, and begins accumulating the labeled trajectory dataset that does not yet exist.
parsed.why_recent_technique_beats_mature_approa: Mature supervised anomaly detection (a CNN classifier or autoencoder trained per object) is blocked here because the problem statement says there is NO labeled time-series of vat trajectories and vats die rarely and unpredictably -- you cannot assemble the hundreds of labeled defect/failure images per vat that classic methods require, and every vat/studio looks different. The new capability is exactly label-free, zero/few-shot detection on UNSEEN objects driven by text prompts and a handful of in-context examples, so it works with the craftsperson's verbal description of 'healthy vs sick' and a few reference photos instead of a curated defect corpus -- removing the per-task training-set blocker that made AI a non-starter for this 0-penetration craft.
parsed.feasibility_now: Pilot-feasible, NOT drop-in. Models are HIGH availability (open-source FADE/IADGPT/VMAD run on a phone-fed RGB stream, no special camera). The honest risk is OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION: the ~89.6% benchmark is on MVTec industrial parts, whereas a foaming, specular, color-shifting dye-vat surface is an unproven texture for zero-shot transfer. So expect to need a short few-shot calibration with a master's labeled 'healthy/declining' images per studio and human-in-the-loop validation over a season before trusting alerts; prompt wording and reference-image curation will need iteration, and smell-only failure modes are invisible to a vision model.
parsed.primary_quote: there is no instrument that tells the craftsperson the vat's health/state, and no labeled time-series of vat trajectories

reasoning_trace.reasoning: The open problem is precisely an absence of labels and instruments, which kills supervised AD; VLMAD's text-prompt + in-context, label-free localization matches a domain where the only 'ground truth' is a master's verbal/sensory description and a handful of reference images. The mature alternative (per-vat supervised model) is blocked by rare, unlabeled failure events. Feasibility is realistic-but-cautious because the foaming specular vat surface is OOD versus the industrial benchmarks, so I scope it as a few-shot-calibrated, human-in-the-loop pilot rather than a turnkey monitor.
reasoning_trace.decision: Use a CLIP/VLM zero-few-shot anomaly detector on phone images of the vat surface to produce an early-warning deviation score + heatmap of vat health, calibrated with a master's few reference photos and bootstrapping the missing labeled trajectory dataset.
